title: Concatenated continuous-drive protection of exchange-based spin-qubit gates
authors: Takuma Kuno, Takeru Utsugi, Andrew J. Ramsay, Hideo Arimoto, Tetsuo Kodera, Hiroyuki Mizuno
abstract: Exchange-based two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits are sensitive to low-frequency detuning noise and control errors. Here, we extend concatenated continuous driving (CCD), implemented by phase modulation of a global microwave drive, to exchange-based SWAP and $\sqrt{\mathrm{SWAP}}$ operations between double-dressed spin qubits and investigate its effectiveness for protecting two-qubit gates. We find that CCD retains strong protection against quasistatic common-mode detuning errors while substantially improving robustness against Rabi-frequency errors and qubit-to-qubit Rabi-frequency mismatch compared with conventional continuous dressing. By contrast, the gate fidelity is impacted by differential detuning errors. By modeling partially correlated quasistatic detuning noise, we further show that the noise-averaged gate fidelity depends strongly on the spatial correlation of the qubit-frequency fluctuations, with positive correlations enhancing CCD protection by suppressing the differential-noise component. These results identify the symmetry and spatial correlation of qubit-frequency noise as key factors governing continuous-drive protection in coupled spin-qubit systems.
summary: This paper investigates methods to protect two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits from environmental noise using Concatenated Continuous Driving (CCD). The authors demonstrate that CCD effectively suppresses common-mode noise but that the gate fidelity remains limited by differential detuning errors. They establish that the symmetry and spatial correlation of noise are critical factors governing the overall robustness of these quantum gates.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving robust, high-fidelity two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, which are highly susceptible to low-frequency detuning noise and control errors.
main_result: Concatenated Continuous Driving (CCD) significantly enhances gate protection against common-mode detuning and Rabi-frequency errors; however, the gate fidelity remains sensitive to differential detuning errors.
method: The authors analyze the system by transforming the Hamiltonian into a second rotating frame and applying perturbative techniques (Schrieffer-Wolff transformation) to analyze error corrections.
model_or_system: The system involves exchange-based two-qubit gates (SWAP, $\sqrt{	ext{SWAP}}$) implemented on double-dressed semiconductor spin qubits using a global phase-modulated microwave drive.
key_observables: Gate fidelity ($F_{	ext{avg}}$), SWAP oscillation population ($P_{\uparrow\downarrow}$), and the dependence of fidelity on detuning ($\delta$) and Rabi-frequency errors ($\Delta$).
important_parameters: Common-mode vs. differential detuning ($\delta_c$ vs. $\delta_d$), Rabi-frequency mismatch, and the spatial correlation of qubit-frequency noise.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA) and assumes that the secondary field, if used, must be identical for both qubits during the exchange pulse.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the SWAP dynamics and gate infidelity under various noise conditions, showing that PMCCD broadens the low-infidelity region against common errors but leaves residual sensitivity to differential detuning.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for robust gates, introducing CCD protection against common errors, deriving the Hamiltonian corrections due to differential detuning, and finally comparing the residual sensitivity to exchange-coupling fluctuations.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed theoretical insights into noise resilience in solid-state quantum computation platforms, specifically quantifying the roles of noise symmetry and spatial correlation in determining gate performance.
